title: Derive the Heisenberg uncertainty principle from Cauchy-Schwarz

problemStatement.formal: For symmetric operators A, B : E →ₗ[ℂ] E on a complex inner product space E, and unit state ψ with ‖ψ‖=1, prove: ‖Aψ − ⟨ψ,Aψ⟩·ψ‖ · ‖Bψ − ⟨ψ,Bψ⟩·ψ‖ ≥ (1/2) · ‖⟨ψ, ABψ − BAψ⟩‖. This is Robertson's uncertainty inequality.
problemStatement.plain: Can the Heisenberg uncertainty principle be derived from the complex Cauchy-Schwarz equality in Lean 4? Yes — via Robertson's 1929 inequality: applying CS to the centered vectors Aψ − ⟨A⟩ψ and Bψ − ⟨B⟩ψ gives ΔA·ΔB ≥ (1/2)|⟨ψ|[A,B]|ψ⟩|.
whyMatters: Shows the Heisenberg uncertainty principle is a pure consequence of Cauchy-Schwarz in Lean 4
Formalizes Robertson's abstract operator formulation covering all physical observables simultaneously
Demonstrates the power of symmetric (self-adjoint) operators: real expectation values are key to cross-term cancellation
Bridges abstract functional analysis and quantum physics without physics axioms

insights: Expectation values of symmetric operators are real: star⟨ψ,Aψ⟩ = ⟨Aψ,ψ⟩ = ⟨ψ,Aψ⟩
Cross terms in ⟪Aψ−⟨A⟩ψ, Bψ−⟨B⟩ψ⟫ − ⟪Bψ−⟨B⟩ψ, Aψ−⟨A⟩ψ⟫ cancel because expVals are real and ⟪ψ,ψ⟫=1
Symmetry of A: ⟪Aψ,Bψ⟫ = star⟪ψ,A(Bψ)⟫ — this reduces cross terms to commutator EV
The Robertson inequality works for any complex IPS, not just L²(ℝ)
Unit state normalization ‖ψ‖=1 is essential for ⟪ψ,ψ⟫=1 in the commutator identity
